content.title: About
content.content: Fruit and vegetable smoothie, non-dairy is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from a blend of fresh fruits, vegetables and plant‑based liquids such as nut milk, coconut water or fruit juices. It contains no dairy, making it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoothies are often prepared with seasonal produce to maximize nutrient retention.
The absence of dairy makes these drinks easier on sensitive stomachs.
Superfoods like spirulina, acai berries, and chia seeds are frequently added for an antioxidant boost.
A properly stored smoothie can stay fresh in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours without major loss of flavor or texture.
In some markets, non‑dairy smoothies are sold as concentrates that are reconstituted with water before consumption.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: The fruit‑vegetable blend provides vitamins A, C, K and minerals such as potassium, magnesium and folate.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber from the produce promotes healthy bowel movements and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients like polyphenols and carotenoids help combat free radicals.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Base liquids such as coconut water or fruit juice aid in maintaining proper fluid balance.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C and other micronutrients boost immune function, especially during cold seasons.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Smoothies may contain nuts, soy or other allergens; individuals with relevant allergies should check the label.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sweet fruits can raise the glycemic index, which may be unsuitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Microbial contamination
items.content: Improper storage above 4 °C for more than 24 hours can allow bacterial growth.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Excessive fiber intake may cause bloating or diarrhea in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the smoothie straight after blending, pour over ice, or use as a base for protein shakes. If desired, sweeten lightly with honey, maple syrup or stevia.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared smoothie in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 24 hours. Shake well before drinking. Discard if the smell, color or taste changes.
